Data Appreciation · Week 5 · Title

Spreadsheets I: cells, rows, columns and formatting

A spreadsheet is a grid for data: learn its parts, enter data cleanly and make it readable.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Data Appreciation · Week 5 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Name a cell by its column and row
  • Enter text, numbers and dates and format them
  • Make a table readable: headers, widths, number formats
Data Appreciation · Week 5 · Idea 1

Understand it

A spreadsheet is a grid.

  • Columns are lettered A, B, C… and run down.
  • Rows are numbered 1, 2, 3… and run across.
  • A cell is where they meet, named column-then-row: B6.
  • The formula bar shows what is really in the selected cell.

Entering data: click a cell, type, press Enter (down) or Tab (right). One value per cell. Put headings in row 1.

Formatting makes it readable without changing the data:

Data Appreciation · Week 5 · Idea 2

Understand it

  • Bold the header row and freeze it (View → Freeze → 1 row).
  • Widen columns (double-click the edge between column letters).
  • Number formats: currency for money, a date format for dates, 0 or 2 decimal places as needed.
  • Align numbers right, text left.

A number formatted as currency is still a number — you can add it up. A number typed as ₦900 text cannot be added: format, don't type the symbol.

The parts of a spreadsheet

Data Appreciation · Week 5 · Key words

Key words

Cell
one box of the grid, named like B6
Column / row
a vertical line of cells (letter) / a horizontal one (number)
Format
how a value looks, without changing the value
Data Appreciation · Week 5 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Open a new spreadsheet in Google Sheets or LibreOffice Calc
  2. Build a shopping budget table with five items
  3. Format the headers, the ₦ column and the widths

Need a hand? Copy the picture's table exactly first, then change the items.

Done early? Add conditional formatting: colour any amount over ₦2,000.

Data Appreciation · Week 5 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • The cell in column C, row 4 is called…
  • Show your formatted budget table: a bold frozen header, readable widths, and the money in currency format.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.
